versions.provenance: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (Version 2024); licensed clinical reference.
versions.introduction: In localized prostate cancer, anatomical TNM staging alone is insufficient for clinical management. The NCCN Risk Stratification system is the universal standard that combines clinical T category, serum PSA, and biopsy Gleason Grade Group to guide therapy selection across active surveillance, surgery, definitive radiation, and androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).

t.label: Non-palpable or palpable tumor involving <= half of one lobe
Palpable tumor involving > half of one lobe (T2b) or bilateral lobes (T2c)
Extraprostatic extension (T3a) or seminal vesicle invasion (T3b)
Tumor fixed or invades adjacent structures (bladder neck, external sphincter, rectum, levator)

m.label: Distant bone, visceral, or non-regional nodal metastases

stageGroups.basis: Active Surveillance standard of care. Treatment deferred unless reclassification.
Active Surveillance preferred. Alternatives: Radical prostatectomy or definitive EBRT/brachytherapy alone.
Radical prostatectomy OR EBRT alone / EBRT + brachytherapy boost. Short-course ADT usually omitted.
EBRT + 4 to 6 months ADT OR Radical prostatectomy + pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND).

stageGroups.t: cT3a OR Grade Group 4-5 OR PSA >20
stageGroups.basis: EBRT + 18 to 24 months ADT (+/- abiraterone) OR Radical prostatectomy + extended PLND by high-volume surgeon.
EBRT + 2 years ADT + 2 years Abiraterone (STAMPEDE protocol) OR Radical prostatectomy + extended PLND in selected patients.
EBRT to prostate and pelvic lymph nodes + 2 years ADT + Abiraterone.
Systemic therapy: ADT + ARPI (Enzalutamide, Apalutamide, Abiraterone) +/- Docetaxel triplet (PEACE-1 / ARASENS).

versions.regionalNodes: Pelvic lymph nodes below the bifurcation of the common iliac arteries: obturator, internal iliac, external iliac, presacral.
versions.histologicGrade: Grade Group 1 (Gleason <=6), Grade Group 2 (Gleason 3+4=7), Grade Group 3 (Gleason 4+3=7), Grade Group 4 (Gleason 8), Grade Group 5 (Gleason 9-10).
versions.histopathologicTypes: Acinar adenocarcinoma (95%), ductal adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine / small cell prostate cancer.
prognosticFactors: Pre-treatment serum PSA and PSA doubling time (PSADT)
Gleason Grade Group (primary vs secondary pattern, presence of cribriform or intraductal carcinoma)
Genomic classifier score (Decipher, Oncotype DX, Prolaris)
Germline and somatic homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene mutations (BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM for PARP inhibitor eligibility)
